ticks.note: An input's initialiser is the value it has before the environment first sets it. I and B are not supplied, so they keep 42 and true; J is supplied (3), which overrides its initialiser. (This is the netlist compiler; the priority-based compiler runs input initialisers after reading the tick-1 inputs, so there J = 42: see input-initial-value-priority.)
The self-loop copies them: x = 42, y = 3, b = true.
Once supplied, the environment's values win: x = 1, b = false.
